newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WOODS LEADS MASTERS BY NINE SHOTS WITH NINE HOLES TO PLAY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS LEADS MASTERS BY NINE SHOTS WITH NINE HOLES TO PLAY.

text.p: Tiger Woods balanced two bogeys with two birdies on the front side to remain nine strokes ahead with nine holes to play Sunday in his march towards an historic Masters title.

The 21-year-old Woods, seeking to become the youngest Masters winner ever and the first non-white player to win one of golf's major championships, birdied the par-5 second hole before wobbling slightly with bogeys at the fifth and seventh holes. He recovered with a birdie at the par-5 eighth.

Italy's Costantino Rocca, paired with Woods, had a birdie and a bogey on the outward half to remain nine shots behind the 21-year-old American in second place at six under par on a breezy day at Augusta National.

After a birdie at the par-5 second hole, Woods stumbled at number five, pulling his approach shot left into the front bunker guarding the green. Woods, on his first bunker shot of the tournament, splashed out a bit strong and needed two putts to take five on the par-4.
The bogey snapped a streak of 37 successive holes at par or better for Woods, whose last bogey had come on the third hole on Friday.

At the short, par-4 seventh, Woods hit a wayward drive into the trees to the left of the fairway. He punched his next shot into the right front bunker, blasted out about eight feet from the pin and took two putts to get down.
Woods appeared to be flirting with danger again at the par-5 eighth hole, but turned potential trouble into a birdie.

Again, he went far left into trees, facing mounds guarding the green. Confronted with a daunting pitch shot, Woods pulled off a beauty, bumping the ball into a grassy rise to slow it down to a trickle feeding towards the cup. He sank his putt for birdie to bring himself back to 15 under par.

Two-time champion Tom Watson, who began the day at four under par, stood at five-under through 11 holes. Tom Kite, the 1992 U.S. Open winner, had also improved by one stroke to five under par after 10.

Woods, who needs a round of 69 to break the Masters scoring record held jointly by Jack Nicklaus and Raymond Floyd, began the day at 15-under-par 201 after shooting 65 on Saturday to pad his lead from three strokes to nine.
